headline: Apple's new chief executive John Ternus said Apple will look at every option to ease the memory chip shortage, which could include Chinese-made memory.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a top Apple executive's remark touches supply, prices and US-China politics; no decision exists.
importance_line: It matters to phone and PC buyers facing higher memory prices and to Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, but Apple has not named any Chinese supplier and US lawmakers oppose it.
summary: Chosun Ilbo reports, citing an interview in Time magazine, that Apple chief executive John Ternus called the memory supply shortage "a serious crisis" and said the company must "review all options"; he did not name Chinese firms, but the paper reads this as leaving room for Chinese memory chips. The Financial Times and the Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year that Apple is testing DRAM from China's CXMT, no deal has been finalised, and seven US senators have asked Apple not to use CXMT or YMTC chips.
notes: Interpretation of Ternus's words is the outlet's, stated as such.
